AN ACT to amend the social services law, the abandoned property law, the arts
and cultural affairs law, the banking law, the criminal procedure law, the

items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6789

SPONSOR: PERSAUD
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the social services law, the abandoned property law, the
arts and cultural affairs law, the banking law, the criminal procedure
law, the debtor and creditor law, the domestic relations law, the educa-
tion law, the executive law, the family court act, the insurance law,
the judiciary law, the mental hygiene law, the public health law, the
public lands law, the private housing finance law, the real property
actions and proceedings law, the real property law, the real property
tax law, the tax law, the facilities development corporation act, and
the medical care facilities finance agency act, in relation to replacing
certain instances of the term mentally retarded or variations of such
term with the term intellectually or developmentally disabled or vari-
ations of such term

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

This bill modernizes language numerous remaining sections of law
containing derogatory references to people living with intellectual or
developmental disabilities.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends subdivision 1 of section 477 of the social services
law, as amended by chapter 550 of the laws of 1978 to replace one
instance of "mentally retarded" with "intellectually or developmentally
disabled.

Section 2 amends section 215 of the abandoned property law, as amended
by chapter 550 of the laws of 1978 to replace one instance of "mental
retardation" with "intellectual or developmental disability".

Section 3 amends paragraph (d) of subdivision 1 of section 35.07 of the
arts and cultural affairs law to replace one instance of "mentally
retarded" with "intellectually or developmentally disabled.

Section 4 amends paragraph (a) of subdivision 3 of section 100 of the
banking law, as amended by chapter 115 of the laws of 1981 to replace a
reference to a "mentally retarded person" with "person with an intellec-
tual or developmental disability".

Section 5 amends subdivision 3 of section 100-a of the banking law, as
amended by chapter 115 of the laws of 1981 to replace a reference to a
"mentally retarded person" with "person with an intellectual or develop-
mental disability".

Section 6 amends paragraph (d) of subdivision 1 and the opening para-
graph subdivision 2 of section 330.20 of the criminal procedure law,
paragraph (d) of subdivision 1 as amended by chapter 672 of the laws of
2019 and the opening paragraph of subdivision 2 as amended by chapter
693 of the laws of 1989, to properly refer to a defendant having an
"intellectual or developmental disability", rather than a defendant who
is "mentally retarded".

Section 7 amends section 251 of the debtor and creditor law, as amended
by chapter 115 of the laws of 1981, to replace a reference to a "mental-
ly retarded person" with "person with an intellectual or developmental
disability".

Section 8 amends section 252 of the debtor and creditor law, as amended
by chapter 115 of the laws of 1981, to replace one instance of "mental
retardation" with "intellectual or developmental disability".

Section 9 amends the third undesignated paragraph of subdivision 1 of
section 13-d of the domestic relations law, as added by chapter 371 of
the laws of 1986, to replace one instance of "mental retardation" with
"intellectual or developmental disability".

Section 10 amends Subdivision 5 of section 115 of the domestic relations
law, as amended by chapter 305 of the laws of 2008, to replace one
instance of "mentally retarded" with "intellectually or developmentally
disabled.

Section 11 amends subdivision (c) of section 140 of the domestic
relations law, as amended by chapter 550 of the laws of 1978, to replace
5 instances of "mentally retarded person" with "person with an intellec-
tual or developmental disability".

Section 12 amends section 142 of the domestic relations law, as amended
by chapter 550 of the laws of 1978, to replace "mentally retarded
person" with "person with an intellectual or developmental disability".

Section 13 amends Paragraph (g) of subdivision 1 of section 414 of the
education law, as amended by chapter 257 of the laws of 1976, to replace
"mentally retarded minors" with "minors with intellectual or develop-
mental disabilities".

Section 14 amends the section heading and subdivisions 1, 2 and 3 of
section 1004-a of the education law, the section heading and subdivi-
sions 1 and 3 as amended by chapter 1014 of the laws of 1974 and subdi-
vision 2 as separately amended by chapters 474 and 475 of the laws of
1978, to replace references to "the mentally retarded, mentally ill and
severely physically handicapped" with "individuals with intellectual or
developmental disabilities, mental illness or a severe physical hand-
icap".

Section 15 amends the opening paragraph of subdivision 8-a of section
1950 of the education law, as added by chapter 762 of the laws of 1972,
to remove "the trainable mentally retarded" and replace with "children
with intellectual or developmental disabilities".

Section 16 amends paragraphs a and b, subparagraphs 1 and 2 of paragraph
c, and subparagraphs 1, 8 and 13 of paragraph d of subdivision 5 of
section 3202 of the education law, paragraph a as added by chapter 47 of
the laws of 1977, and as renumbered by chapter 563 of the laws of 1980,
paragraph b as amended by section 26 of part B of chapter 57 of the laws
of 2007, subparagraphs 1 and 2 of paragraph c and subparagraphs 1 and 13
of paragraph d as amended by chapter 672 of the laws of 2019, and
subparagraph 8 of paragraph d as added by chapter 721 of the laws of
1979, and as renumbered by chapter 57 of the laws of 1993 to replace 8
instances of "the mentally retarded" with "individuals with intellectual
or developmental disabilities"


Section 17 amends subclause (iii) of clause (c) of subparagraph 4 of
paragraph b of subdivision 1 of section 4402 of the education law, as
amended by chapter 378 of the laws of 2007, to replace "mental retarda-
tion" with "an intellectual or a developmental disability".

Section 18 amends subclause (iii) of clause (c) of subparagraph 4 of
paragraph b of subdivision 1 of section 4402 of the education law, as
amended by chapter 600 of the laws of 1994, to replace "mental retarda-
tion" with "an intellectual or a developmental disability".

Section 19 amends subdivision 4 of section 4403 of the education law, as
amended by chapter 53 of the laws of 1986, to replace "mental retarda-
tion" with "intellectual" in reference to certain state facilities.

Section 20 section 4809 of the education law, as amended by chapter 550
of the laws of 1978, to replace "mentally retarded" with "living with an
intellectual or developmental disability".

Section 21 amends paragraph a of subdivision 3 of section 6507 of the
education law, as amended by chapter 672 of the laws of 2019, to modern-
ize references to prescribed coursework pertaining to abuses of "indi-
viduals with intellectual or developmental disabilities", rather than
"individuals with mental retardation".

Section 22 amends subparagraph (i) of paragraph (a) of subdivision 1 of
section 509 of the executive law, as added by chapter 659 of the laws of
1977 and renumbered by chapter 465 of the laws of 1992, to modernize a
reference to a child "living with mental illness or an intellectual or
developmental disability" rather than being referred to as "mentally ill
or retarded".

Section 23 amends subdivision (b) of section 115 of the family court
act, as amended by chapter 281 of the laws of 1980, to modernize a
reference to "intellectually or developmentally disabled" children rath-
er than being referred to as "mentally defective or retarded".

Section 24 amends item (i) of subparagraph (A) of paragraph 4 of
subsection (a) of section 3216 of the insurance law, as amended by chap-
ter 219 of the laws of 2011, to properly refer to an "intellectual or
developmental disability" rather than "mental retardation".

Section 25 amends Subparagraph (A) of paragraph 4 and subparagraph (B)
of paragraph 5 of subsection (c) of section 3216 of the insurance law,
subparagraph (A) of paragraph 4 as amended by chapter 93 of the laws of
1989, and subparagraph (B) of paragraph 5 as amended by section 46-b of
part D of chapter 56 of the laws of 2013, to modernize two references to
an "intellectual or developmental disability" rather than "mental retar-
dation"

Section 26 amends Item (ii) of subparagraph (A) of paragraph 1 of
subsection (f) of section 4235 of the insurance law, as amended by chap-
ter 219 of the laws of 2011, to modernize a reference to "intellectual
or developmental disability" rather than "mental retardation"

Section 27 Item (ii) of subparagraph (A) of paragraph 1 and paragraph 3
of subsection (d) of section 4304 of the insurance law, as amended by
chapter 219 of the laws of 2011, to modernize two references to an

"intellectual or developmental disability" rather than "mental retarda-
tion"

Section 28 amends item (ii) of subparagraph (A) of paragraph 1 of
subsection (c) of section 4305 of the insurance law, as amended by chap-
ter 219 of the laws of 2011, to modernize a reference to "intellectual
or developmental disability" rather than "mental retardation"

Section 29 amends paragraph a of subdivision 1 of section 35 of the
judiciary law, as amended by chapter 817 of the laws of 1986, to modern-
ize a reference to "intellectual or developmental disability" rather
than "mental retardation"; and to modernize a reference to a person who
is "intellectually or developmentally disabled" rather than being
referred to as "mentally retarded".

Section 30 renames the article heading of article 15 of title C of the
mental 12 hygiene law, as renumbered by chapter 978 of the laws of 1977,
to: "ADMISSION OF PEOPLE WITH INTELLECTUAL OR DEVELOPMENTAL DISABILITIES
TO SCHOOLS".

Section 31 amends paragraphs 1 and 2 of subdivision (a) of section 41.17
of the mental hygiene law, as amended by chapter 471 of the laws of
1980, to cease the use of "mentally retarded" and refer to people who
are "intellectually or developmentally disabled".

Section 32 amends Paragraph (i) of subdivision (b) of section 41.18 of
the mental hygiene law, as amended by chapter 376 of the laws of 1991,
to replace "mentally retarded or developmentally disabled persons" with
"people with intellectual or developmental disabilities".

Section 33 renames the The article heading of article 75 of title E of
the mental hygiene law to: "COMMUNITY MENTAL HEALTH SERVICES AND DEVEL-
OPMENTAL DISABILITIES SERVICES COMPANIES"

Section 34 amends subdivisions 1, 2 and 4 of section 75.05 of the mental
hygiene law, subdivision 4 as amended by chapter 570 of the laws of
1982, to replace "mental retardation" with "developmental disabilities"
in the definitions of "company", "project" and "project cost", respec-
tively.

Section 35 amends subdivision 1 of section 2581 of the public health
law, as amended by chapter 231 of the laws of 2010, to modernize the
definition of "children with physical disabilities" by striking "mental
retardation" and replacing with "intellectual or developmental disabili-
ty".

Section 36 amends the opening paragraph of subdivision 3 of section
2994-b of the public health law, as amended by chapter 708 of the laws
of 2019, to affirm that services are provided for "an intellectual or
developmental disability", rather than for "mental retardation or a
developmental disability".

Section 37 amends the section heading and subdivision I of section 34 of
the public lands law, as amended by chapter 703 of the laws of 1994, to
refer to unappropriated land transfers as being for the purpose of
"developmental disabilities facilities" rather than "mental retardation
facilities".

Section 38 amends subdivision 8 of section 41 of the private housing
finance law, as amended by chapter 264 of the laws of 1970, to refer, in
six instances, to "developmental disabilities facilities" rather than
"mental retardation facilities".

Section 39 amends subdivisions 6-d, 14 and 14-a of section 42 of the
private housing finance law, subdivision 6-d as added by chapter 380 of
the laws of 1972, subdivision 14 as amended by chapter 281 of the laws
of 1970 and subdivision 14-a as added by chapter 570 of the laws of
1982, to modify properly reference, in 13 instances, "developmental
disabilities" rather than "mental retardation".

Section 40 amends paragraphs (a) and (d) of subdivision 15 of section 44
of the private housing finance law, as amended by chapter 195 of the
laws of 1973, to rename "mental retardation services project bonds or
notes" as "developmental disabilities services project bonds or notes".

Section 41 amends paragraphs (a), (b), (c) and (d) of subdivision 1,
subdivision 2, paragraphs (a), (b), (c) and (d) of subdivision 12,
subdivision 13 and paragraphs (a), (b) and (c) of subdivision 16 of
section 47 of the private housing finance law, paragraphs (a), (b) and
(d) of subdivision 1 and subdivision 2 as amended by chapter 215 of the
laws of 1990, paragraph (c) of subdivision 1 as amended by chapter 127
of the laws of 2019, paragraphs (a) and (d) of subdivision 12 as amended
by chapter 365 of the laws of 1973 and subdivision 13 as amended by
chapter 195 of the laws of 1973, paragraphs (b) and (c) of subdivision
12 as amended by chapter 38 of the laws of 1976 and paragraphs (a), (b)
and (c) of subdivision 16 as added by chapter 570 of the laws of 1982,
to replace 68 instances of "mental retardation" with "developmental
disabilities" in the context of capital reserve funds for such purposes.

Section 42 amends paragraphs a and b of subdivision 1 of section 47-b of
the private housing finance law, as amended by chapter 471 of the laws
of 1980, modernize definitions including derogatory language:  (1)
"community mental health and retardation facility" and any similar
references therein are replaced with "community mental health and devel-
opmental disabilities facility"; (2) includes "community mental health
and developmental disabilities facility" within the definition of
"mental hygiene facility".

Section 43 amends paragraphs a and b of subdivision 7 of section 47-c of
the private housing finance law, paragraph a as amended by chapter 607
of the laws of 1970, and paragraph b as amended by chapter 433 of the
laws of 1968, to replace numerous instances of "retardation" with
"developmental disabilities" in various contexts.

Section 44 amends subdivision 5 of section 55 of the private housing
finance law, as amended by chapter 195 of the laws of 1973, to replace
"mental retardation" with "developmental disabilities" in reference to
certain mortgage loans.

Section 45 amends subdivision 1 of section 1531 of the real property
actions and proceedings law, as amended by chapter 550 of the laws of
1978, to refer to a person "with an intellectual or developmental disa-
bility" rather than a "mentally retarded person".



Section 46 amends paragraph c of subdivision 1 of section 1515 of the
real property actions and proceedings law, as amended by chapter 550 of
the laws of 1978,

Section 47 amends subdivisions 1, 3 and 4 of section 1651 of the real
property actions and proceedings law, as amended by chapter 115 of the
laws of 1981, replaces six instances of "mentally retarded person" with
"person with an intellectual or developmental disability".

Section 48 amends section 11 of the real property law, as amended by
chapter 550 of the laws of 1978, in referring to "capacity to transfer
real property", a reference to "mentally retarded person", replacing
with a "person with an intellectual or developmental disability".

Section 49 amends paragraph (a) of subdivision 1 of section 422 of the
real property tax law, as amended by chapter 409 of the laws of 1993, to
replace a reference to "(the) mentally retarded" with "intellectually or
developmentally disabled".

Section 50 amends paragraph (k) of subdivision 1 of section 364-j of the
social services law, as amended by chapter 649 of the laws of 1996, to
properly refer to "intellectual or developmental disabilities", rather
than "mental retardation" in the context of certain special care.

Section 51 amends subdivision 4 of section 365-g of the social services
law, as amended by section 31 of part C of chapter 58 of the laws of
2008, to modernize the reference to "intellectual or developmental disa-
bilities services" rather than "mental retardation and developmental
disabilities services".

Section 52 amends subparagraph (ii) of paragraph (d) of subdivision 6 of
section 367-a of the social services law, as added by chapter 41 of the
laws of 1992, to modernize the reference to "intellectual or develop-
mental disabilities services" rather than "mental retardation and devel-
opmental disabilities services".

Section 53 amends paragraph (p) of subdivision 1 of section 261 of the
tax law, as 24 amended by chapter 365 of the laws of 2005, to properly
refer to a "community mental health and developmental disabilities
facility" rather than a "community mental health and retardation facili-
ty"

Section 54 amends subdivisions 10 and 19 of section 3 of section 1 of
chapter 359 of the laws of 1968, constituting the facilities development
corporation act, subdivision 10 as amended by section 1 of part N of
chapter 59 of the laws of 2016 and subdivision 19 as amended by section
1 of part H of chapter 58 of the laws of 2008, to update the definitions
of "mental hygiene facility" and "voluntary agency" to replace refer-
ences to "mental retardation" with "developmental disabilities"

Section 55 amends The first undesignated paragraph of section 2 of
section 1 of chapter 359 of the laws of 1968, constituting the facili-
ties development I corporation act, as separately amended by chapters
195 and 658 of the 2 laws of 1973, to modernize a reference to "people
with intellectual or developmental disabilities" by removing "mentally
retarded".


Section 56 amends the third undesignated paragraph of section 2 of
section 1 of chapter 359 of the laws of 1968, constituting the facili-
ties development corporation act, as amended by chapter 547 of the laws
of 1979, to replace references to "mental retardation", "mentally
retarded" with "developmental disabilities" and "developmentally disa-
bled", respectively, in the context of state facilities.

Section 57 amends paragraph a of subdivision 8 and subdivision 13 of
section 5 of section 1 of chapter 359 of the laws of 1968, constituting
the facilities development corporation act, paragraph a of subdivision 8
as amended by chapter 58 of the laws of 1987 and subdivision 13 as
amended by chapter 723 of the laws of 1993, by replacing several
instances of "retardation" with "developmental disabilities" in the
context of state facilities.

Section 58 amends subdivisions 3, 4 and 5 of section 6 of section 1 of
chapter 359 of the laws of 1968, constituting the facilities development
corporation act, subdivisions 3 and 4 as amended by chapter 547 of the
laws of 1979 and subdivision 5 as amended by chapter 351 of the laws of
1985, by replacing instances of "retardation" with "developmental disa-
bilities" in the context of state facilities.

Section 59 amends paragraphs b and c of subdivision 1 of section 9 of
section 1 of chapter 359 of the laws of 1968, constituting the facili-
ties development corporation act, paragraph b as amended by chapter 58
of the laws of 1987 and paragraph c as amended by chapter 547 of the
laws of 1979, by replacing instances of "retardation" with "develop-
mental disabilities" in the context of state facilities.

Section 60 amends the opening paragraph of subparagraph (i) and subpara-
graph (ii) of paragraph b of subdivision 2 of section 9 of section 1 of
chapter 359 of the laws of 1968, constituting the facilities development
corporation act, the opening paragraph of subparagraph (i) as amended by
chapter 166 of the laws of 1991 and subparagraph (ii) as amended by
chapter 658 of the laws of 1973, by replacing instances of "retardation"
with "developmental disabilities" in the context of state facilities.

Section 61 Paragraphs a and b of subdivision 3 of section 9 of section 1
of chapter 359 of the laws of 1968, constituting the facilities develop-
ment corporation act, paragraph a as amended by chapter 723 of the laws
of 1993 and paragraph b as amended by section 48 of part TTT of chapter
59 of the laws of 2019, by replacing instances of "retardation" with
"developmental disabilities" in the context of state facilities and by
updating the name of the Office of Addiction Services & Supports.

Section 62 amends the fifth undesignated paragraph of subdivision 5 of
section 9 of section 1 of chapter 359 of the laws of 1968, constituting
the facilities development corporation act, as amended by chapter 58 of
the laws of 1987, to modernize a reference to "community mental health
and developmental disabilities facilities".

Section 63 Subdivision 6 of section 9 of section 1 of chapter 359 of the
laws of 1968, constituting the facilities development corporation act,
paragraphs a and b as amended by chapter 58 of the laws of 1987, by
replacing instances of "retardation" with "developmental disabilities"
in the context of state facilities and by updating the name of the
Office of Addiction Services & Supports.

Section 64 amends the fifth undesignated paragraph of section 2 of
section 1 of chapter 392 of the laws of 1973, constituting the medical
care facilities finance agency act, as added by chapter 58 of the laws
of 1987, to replace "mentally retarded or developmentally disabled" with
"intellectually or developmentally disabled.

Section 65 amends Subdivisions 4 and 6 of section 5-a of section 1 of
chapter 392 of the laws of 1973, constituting the medical care facili-
ties finance agency act, subdivision 4 as amended by chapter 389 of the
laws of 1987, and subdivision 6 as amended by chapter 672 of the laws of
2019, to replace several references to -mentally retarded" with "intel-
lectually or".

Section 66 amends paragraph a of subdivision 1 of section 9-a of section
1 of 21 chapter 392 of the laws of 1973, constituting the medical care
facilities finance agency act, as amended by chapter 166 of the laws of
1991, by replacing instances of "retardation" with "developmental disa-
bilities" in the context of state facilities.

Section 67 specifies that any use of the terms "intellectual disability"
or "intellectual or developmental disability" or equivalent expressions
thereof mean "developmental disability" as defined in subdivision 22 of
section 1.03 of the Mental Hygiene Law.

Section 68 establishes an immediate effective date with exceptions
pertaining to two sections.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

In 2011, less than one year following the enactment of Rosa's Law (Pub.
L. 111-256), New York State took decisive action (Chapter 37, Laws of
2011) to designate the Office for People with Developmental Disabilities
(OPWDD) and move away from derogatory references to New Yorkers living
with disabilities. Several state laws enacted since 2011 have included
conforming changes in various sections of law, but references to "mental
retardation" and "mentally retarded" and "the mentally retarded" contin-
ue to appear in the very laws that establish benefits and services for
New Yorkers living with disabilities.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

This is new legislation.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS TO STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
Immediately with exceptions pertaining to one expiring section of law
and one section of law not yet in effect.

JUSTIFICATION:

In 2011, less than one year following the enactment of Rosa's Law (Pub.
L. 111-256), New York State took decisive action (Chapter 37, Laws of
2011) to designate the Office for People with Developmental Disabilities
(OPWDD) and move away from derogatory references to New Yorkers living
with disabilities. Several state laws enacted since 2011 have included
conforming changes in various sections of law, but references to "mental
retardation" and "mentally retarded" and "the mentally retarded" contin-
ue to appear in the very laws.that establish benefits and services for
New Yorkers living with disabilities.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

This is new legislation.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS TO STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
Immediately with exceptions pertaining to one expiring section of law
and one section of law not yet in effect.

summary: Replaces certain instances of the term mentally retarded or variations of such term with the term developmentally disabled or variations of such term.
